title: Orioles claim Robert Jr. off waivers from Mets
dek: Baltimore acquired outfielder Luis Robert Jr., 29, off outright waivers from the Mets on August 31. The Orioles are one game behind the Guardians for a wild-card berth despite a sub-.500 record. Robert Jr. did not report to the Mets before the claim.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: The Orioles claimed Luis Robert Jr., 29, off waivers from the Mets as the team pursues a September postseason push.
bottom_line: The specifics of Robert Jr.'s salary, contract status, and immediate eligibility with Baltimore will determine whether this acquisition has time to meaningfully impact the Orioles' postseason odds. His willingness to report to the team is the immediate prerequisite.
body: The Baltimore Orioles claimed outfielder Luis Robert Jr., 29, off outright waivers from the Mets on August 31, according to MLB.com. The move adds depth to the Orioles' roster as they enter the final stretch of the regular season one game behind the Guardians for a wild-card berth, despite carrying a sub-.500 record.

Robert Jr. did not report to the Mets before being placed on waivers, according to MLB.com. The circumstances surrounding his non-reporting remain unclear, as does whether he will join the Orioles' roster.
The Orioles announced they are targeting a September push toward postseason contention. The claim represents an attempt to bolster the outfield ahead of the final month of competition.
